dimensions.assessment: Affects federally insured depository institutions and credit unions with assets of $6 billion or less, their regulators, and their management personnel.
dimensions.evidence: well managed and well capitalized insured depository institution with $6,000,000,000 or less in consolidated assets

dimensions.assessment: Streamlines federal oversight by alternating examination scopes and combining safety, soundness, and compliance exams upon request, reducing routine regulatory friction.
dimensions.evidence: the next examination of the insured depository institution by the appropriate Federal banking agency shall be a limited-scope examination

dimensions.assessment: Modifies agency examination schedules and reporting requirements, with negligible direct federal spending or revenue impact stated.
dimensions.evidence: In its annual report to Congress, each Federal banking agency shall include--information on how the agency is complying with paragraphs (11) and (12)

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and the Federal Credit Union Act to alter statutory examination mandates and agency rulemaking duties.
dimensions.evidence: Section 10(d) of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (12 U.S.C. 1820(d)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Creates permanent statutory changes to federal banking agency examination cycles and ongoing annual reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: In its annual report to Congress, each Federal banking agency shall include...

missing_information: The precise number of financial institutions meeting the $6 billion asset threshold and well-managed criteria is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The SMART Act of 2025 reduces regulatory examination burdens and combines examination procedures for well-capitalized and well-managed insured depository institutions and credit unions with $6 billion or less in consolidated assets.
